text: At 65 minutes, Seabrook Town implemented a pressing trigger by raising their press intensity from 0.66 to 0.84 and line height from 0.6 to 0.72, combined with a shift to more direct play (directness 0.42 to 0.57) to chase the game and disrupt Harbour City's patient short-passing build-up [#1361]. Despite increasing their PPDA pressure and adopting a higher defensive line, Seabrook's field tilt dropped sharply from 70.7% to 45.7%, signaling Harbour City’s effective rest-defence and possession retention under pressure [#1361]. Seabrook's offensive metrics, including xG (0.56 to 0.47) and box touches (12 to 7), declined, showing that the increase in directness did not create more progressive passes or better scoring opportunities against Harbour City's compact 4-2-3-1 defensive shape [#1361]. The tactical adjustment thus triggered a transition in control but did not yield the desired territorial or chance dominance.
